enriched.summary: The lesson focuses on the Present Continuous tense, including its affirmative, negative, and interrogative forms, as well as its various uses. Additionally, vocabulary related to retirement and trends is introduced, along with practical examples for sentence formation.
mainTopics: Vocabulary related to trends and retirement

vocabulary.definition: used to describe a situation or quality that is increasing over time.
examples: The weather is becoming more and more unpredictable.
People are investing more and more in sustainable energy.

vocabulary.definition: having stopped working permanently, typically due to age.
examples: My father is retired and enjoys gardening.
Many retired people travel the world.

vocabulary.definition: the period of life when someone stops working permanently.
examples: She is saving money for her retirement.
Retirement can be a time to explore new hobbies.

vocabulary.definition: to stop working permanently due to age or other reasons.
examples: He plans to retire at the age of 65.
Many people dream of retiring early.

vocabulary.definition: the sale of goods to the public in relatively small quantities for use or consumption.
examples: I’m finishing a project with a big retail company.
The retail industry is growing rapidly.

grammar.explanation: The Present Continuous tense is used to describe actions happening at the moment of speaking, temporary situations, ongoing events, or trends and changes.
rules: Formed with the present tense of the verb 'to be' (am/is/are) + verb ending in '-ing'.
Use 'not' to form negatives (e.g., I am not working).
In questions, invert the subject and 'to be' (e.g., Are you working?).
examples: We’re living with my mother because we’re waiting for the keys to the new apartment.
I’m finishing a project with a big retail company.
The weather is becoming more and more unpredictable.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to use 'am/is/are' in the sentence (e.g., 'I working' instead of 'I am working').
Using the base form of the verb without '-ing' (e.g., 'He is work' instead of 'He is working').
Confusing Present Continuous with Simple Present for ongoing actions (e.g., 'I study now' instead of 'I’m studying now').

practiceQuestions.question: Form a sentence: Liam / save / money / because he wants to buy a car.
practiceQuestions.answer: Liam is saving money because he wants to buy a car.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The action is happening now and will continue temporarily.

practiceQuestions.question: Ask a question: which room / the baby / sleep / in?
practiceQuestions.answer: Which room is the baby sleeping in?
practiceQuestions.explanation: This is a 'wh-' question formed by inverting the subject and the verb 'to be'.

practiceQuestions.question: Correct the mistake: He working on a project.
practiceQuestions.answer: He is working on a project.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The auxiliary verb 'is' is missing before the '-ing' verb.

culturalNotes: The concept of retirement varies across cultures. In some countries, people retire as early as 55, while in others, they may work until their 70s.
Retail is a significant part of the global economy and influences consumer behavior in various ways.
studyTips: Practice forming sentences using the Present Continuous to describe what you or others are doing right now.
Memorize the common uses of the Present Continuous to avoid confusing it with the Simple Present.
Use flashcards to learn vocabulary words and their translations.
originalExamples: The little girl is having ice cream with her older sister. (A menina está tomando sorvete com sua irmã mais velha.)
Liam is saving money because he wants to buy a car. (Liam está economizando dinheiro porque ele quer comprar um carro.)
You aren’t listening to me. (Você não está me ouvindo.)
My parents are looking for a new apartment. (Meus pais estão procurando um novo apartamento.)
The victim isn’t cooperating with the police. (A vítima não está cooperando com a polícia.)
Lucas and I are planning a trip to Japan. (Lucas e eu estamos planejando uma viagem ao Japão.)
I’m cooking fish for dinner. (Eu estou cozinhando peixe para o jantar.)
The water is boiling. You can put the pasta now. (A água está fervendo. Você pode colocar o macarrão agora.)
Henry isn’t training because he has health problems. (Henry não está treinando porque ele tem problemas de saúde.)
It isn’t raining now. We can go to the park. (Não está chovendo agora. Podemos ir ao parque.)
Are you crying? (Você está chorando?)
Is your father recovering well after the operation? (Seu pai está se recuperando bem após a operação?)
Are the engineers trying to find a solution? (Os engenheiros estão tentando encontrar uma solução?)
Is the baby sleeping? (O bebê está dormindo?)
Are we doing the right thing? (Estamos fazendo a coisa certa?)
Is William studying for his exams? (William está estudando para os exames?)
Are you eating my pizza? (Você está comendo minha pizza?)
Is the client paying by credit card? (O cliente está pagando com cartão de crédito?)
Are your friends winning the match? (Seus amigos estão ganhando a partida?)
Is Tom running in the race? (O Tom está correndo na corrida?)
Is Barcelona winning the game? (O Barcelona está ganhando o jogo?)
